question: Where was the FIRST surgery under anaesthesia?

post.premise: A dentist, a sponge of ether and a tumour cut out in silence
post.bait: England, France or the USA — which did you pick? 👇
post.sources_line: Massachusetts General Hospital; Linda Hall Library; Britannica; The Conversation

youtube.title: Where was the first surgery under anaesthesia? A dentist held the sponge 😴
youtube.description:
England, France or the third one? Before this day, surgery meant being held down. Then a dentist in a hospital amphitheatre put a patient to sleep, a surgeon cut a tumour from his neck, and the man felt nothing. Another doctor had quietly done it 4 years earlier and told no one.
Guess before the map lights up, then see the city, the two rival dates, and how fast the news crossed the Atlantic.
Which flag did you back?

intent: A single operating theatre, then the quiet rival four years earlier, then the news racing across the ocean: the day pain was switched off.

v04.text: The USA. On 16 October 1846 at Massachusetts General in Boston a dentist put a patient to sleep with ether.

v05.text: Morton held the sponge; John Warren cut a tumour from Gilbert Abbott's neck. He felt nothing at all.

v06.text: But Crawford Long of Jefferson, Georgia had already done it 4 years earlier, unpublished.

v07.text: Within 2 months London heard, and Robert Liston amputated a leg under ether that December.

research.topic: First surgery under anaesthesia: the USA — the first public demonstration of ether anaesthesia at Massachusetts General Hospital, Boston, 16 October 1846 (Morton/Warren/Abbott); Crawford Long's earlier unpublished use in Jefferson, Georgia, 30 March 1842; Liston's first ether operation in London, 21 December 1846.

myths.myth: Anaesthesia was a British invention because Britain led 19th-century medicine.
myths.reality: The first public demonstration was in Boston in October 1846, and an American doctor in Georgia had used ether privately in 1842; London followed in December 1846.

landscape.our_gap: Feed clips tell the Ether Dome story as a talking head; nobody pins the theatre, sets the two rival American dates side by side and then draws the news crossing the Atlantic on a moving map.

mgh_etherdome.title: The Ether Dome at Mass General — Russell Museum
mgh_etherdome.notes: William T. G. Morton made history on 16 October 1846 in MGH's surgical amphitheatre, now the Ether Dome, demonstrating the first public surgery using anaesthetic ether; John Collins Warren operated; 8,000+ operations performed there 1821–1868

lindahall.title: Scientist of the Day — Ether Dome, Massachusetts General Hospital
lindahall.notes: 16 October 1846: Warren removed a tumour from the neck of Boston housepainter Edward Gilbert Abbott while Morton administered sulfuric ether; Crawford Long had used ether in Georgia in 1842; the day became 'Ether Day'

conversation_long.title: The surprising (and Long) story of the first use of ether in surgery
conversation_long.notes: Crawford Long of Jefferson, Georgia, used ether on 30 March 1842 but did not publish until 1849; Morton's public demonstration at MGH on 16 October 1846 is the date history recorded

britannica_anes.title: Anesthetic — history
britannica_anes.notes: Long used ether in 1842 in Georgia; Morton's public demonstration in Boston in October 1846; ether used in London by Robert Liston on 21 December 1846

rcs_liston.publisher: Royal College of Surgeons of England
rcs_liston.title: Robert Liston and the first operation under ether in Britain
rcs_liston.notes: Liston amputated a leg at University College Hospital, London, under ether on 21 December 1846 — the first such operation in Europe, about two months after Boston

ucl_liston.title: Liston and the first anaesthetic in Europe
ucl_liston.notes: on 21 December 1846 Robert Liston performed the first operation under ether in Europe at UCH, London

long_1849.publisher: Southern Medical and Surgical Journal (1849) via NIH / PubMed Central
long_1849.title: An account of the first use of sulphuric ether by inhalation as an anaesthetic in surgical operations — C. W. Long, 1849
long_1849.notes: Long's own 1849 account: ether given to James Venable for removal of a neck tumour at Jefferson, Georgia, on 30 March 1842; not published until 1849
